title: CLARITree: Cholesky and Lookahead Accelerations for Regression with Interpretable Piecewise Linear Trees
claim: Greedy methods are fast but inaccurate and optimal methods are too slow; ours reaches near-optimal accuracy at low runtime.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right: schematic objective-vs-runtime plane, then data-fit scatter
description: Two panels. The left is a schematic plot titled 'Training Objective vs. Runtime', with Objective on the y-axis and Runtime on the x-axis. Three triangle markers stand for methods. Greedy sits at top left (MSE 3.37, 7e-4 sec) and carries a red X. STreeD (Optimal) is a dashed triangle at the right (MSE 1.49, 600 sec, 'Out of time limitation'), with a red X at the bottom right. CLARITree (Ours) is at the bottom left (MSE 0.75, 0.16 sec), marked by a blue check at the corner. MSE values and times are colored blue for good and orange-red for bad. The right panel is a scatter plot of Feature against Target. Orange points show the original piecewise-linear data, and dark blue points show CLARITree's fitted line segments, which follow the data closely. A legend box gives Test R² 0.97. The eye goes first to the large left title and the red and blue marks.
caption: An illustration of CLARITree on a synthetic piecewise-linear dataset. Training objective versus runtime is shown. Greedy trees are fast but suboptimal, while optimal trees take too long to run. CLARITree provides a strong trade-off, achieving near-optimal performance with much lower runtime. The reported results include both train and test performance. Test performance: Greedy (MSE $=15.41$, $R^2=0.88$); CLARITree (MSE $=4.03$, $R^2=0.97$); STreeD (MSE $=13.72$, $R^2=0.89$)
abstract: Regression trees are among the most interpretable yet expressive model classes in machine learning. Historically, greedy induction has been the dominant approach for constructing well-performing regression trees. While optimal methods based on dynamic programming and branch-and-bound exist, they are computationally prohibitive for general linear regression trees, despite often achieving substantially better performance than greedy approaches. Recent work has shown that specialized lookahead strategies can dramatically improve runtime while maintaining near-optimal performance, primarily in classification settings. In this work, we develop a novel algorithm for near-optimal, sparse, piecewise linear regression trees that combines a lookahead-style search strategy with efficient rank-one Cholesky updates of the Gram matrix. We demonstrate, both theoretically and empirically, that our method achieves a favorable trade-off between computational efficiency, predictive accuracy, and sparsity, and scales significantly better than the current state of the art.
